result: Silence has become a luxury item, rarer than gold and far more difficult to mine. We hoard our noise—the constant hum of podcasts, the algorithmic drip of social media, the endless pinging of notifications—as if a quiet moment were a vacuum that might swallow us whole. But silence is not empty. It is a fertile void, a space where thoughts can stretch their limbs without hitting the walls of someone else's opinion. When I sit in genuine quiet, I notice the fridge's low mechanical sigh, the distant bark of a dog, the rustle of my own breath moving through my chest like tide through a cave. These small sounds are the texture of reality, usually drowned out by the digital roar. It is in this stillness that the mind finally stops performing and starts being. Unanswered questions rise to the surface, not demanding solutions, but simply requesting acknowledgment. Old memories drift by, wearing softer colors than they did in the moment. And sometimes, if I am patient enough, a single clear thought emerges—a thought that feels like it has always been there, waiting for the noise to subside, waiting for the stage to be empty so it could take its bow. I do not seek silence to escape the world. I seek it to remember what the world feels like when it is not shouting at me. I seek it to hear myself thinking.
